title: Cost-effectiveness evaluation of individual vs. group psychological treatment for emotional disorders
author: Angel Aguilera-Martin
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bx2npqde

steps.title: Recruit participants at three sites
steps.instruction: Begin recruitment on September 2021 at the three primary‑care locations in Córdoba province: (1) Carlos Castilla del Pino Health Centre, (2) Levante Sur Dr. Manuel Barragán Solís Health Centre, and (3) Community Mental Health Unit of Montilla.

steps.title: Screen, obtain consent, and apply criteria
steps.instruction: General practitioners invite patients they suspect of an emotional disorder (ED) to join the study; obtain written informed consent; a blinded assessor‑investigator administers the screening instruments (PHQ‑4) and, if positive, the diagnostic scales PHQ‑9, GAD‑7, PHQ‑PD and PHQ‑15 to determine disorder type and severity. Include only adults aged 18‑65 with mild or moderate ED (per PHQ scores). Exclude anyone with a severe mental illness, a recent severe suicide attempt, or high impairment on the SDI. Return ineligible patients to their GP.

steps.title: Determine required sample size
steps.instruction: Plan to enrol a total of 128 participants.

steps.title: Randomise eligible participants
steps.instruction: A non‑assessor investigator uses a computer‑generated randomisation list to allocate participants in a 1:1:1 ratio to one of three experimental arms: group brief transdiagnostic CBT (group tCBT), individual brief transdiagnostic CBT (individual tCBT), or treatment‑as‑usual (TAU).

steps.title: Deliver group brief transdiagnostic CBT
steps.instruction: Provide the group tCBT intervention (adapted Unified Protocol) over 12‑16 weeks: seven 90‑minute sessions delivered by a clinical psychologist not involved in assessments, with 8‑10 participants per group. Sessions are weekly at first and become bi‑weekly as the programme progresses. Supply supporting materials: theory documents, a CD for progressive muscle relaxation, self‑recording sheets, and access to the therapy website www.desordenesemocionales.es.

steps.title: Deliver individual brief transdiagnostic CBT
steps.instruction: Provide the individual tCBT intervention (adapted from the group version) with a minimum of 6 and a maximum of 8 sessions, each lasting 30‑60 minutes, delivered by a clinical psychologist not involved in assessments. Session number, length and content are personalised to the participant.

steps.title: Provide treatment‑as‑usual (TAU)
steps.instruction: Allow participants in the TAU arm to receive the usual primary‑care care from their GP: a face‑to‑face consultation that rarely exceeds 10 minutes, typically pharmacological treatment (antidepressants, anxiolytics, hypnotics, sedatives) or practical advice. The first GP visit counts as part of recruitment; no therapeutic help is given until allocation. If the GP recommends any psychological treatment, exclude the participant to avoid contamination. TAU continues until the GP judges the patient recovered; no fixed number of sessions.

steps.title: Conduct outcome assessments
steps.instruction: Administer the same set of instruments (PHQ‑4, PHQ‑9, GAD‑7, PHQ‑PD, PHQ‑15, SDI) after each intervention is finished (post‑intervention) and again at 6‑month and 12‑month follow‑up visits to evaluate durability of effects.

steps.title: Collect cost‑related data
steps.instruction: Gather direct and indirect cost information from medical records and ad‑hoc questionnaires covering the period from 3 months before inclusion to 12 months after the intervention ends.

substeps.instruction: Direct costs: add medication costs (price per mg from Vademecum International × daily dose in mg × number of treatment days), costs of medical tests and other health services (fees from the Andalusian Health Service website), and personnel costs (GP and clinical‑psychologist salaries; treat a group‑psychotherapy session as a GP consultation for costing).
Indirect costs: multiply the number of ED‑related sick‑leave days by the daily minimum salary at the time; add any replacement‑worker costs if applicable.
Total cost = direct costs + indirect costs.

steps.title: Perform statistical effectiveness analyses
steps.instruction: Use SPSS Statistics to analyse effectiveness data with both intention‑to‑treat and per‑protocol approaches. After checking intra‑ and inter‑group homogeneity, analyse changes over time (baseline, post‑intervention, 6‑ and 12‑month follow‑ups) with linear mixed models. Compute Cohen’s d effect sizes and adjust for the number of sessions attended. Estimate the proportion of participants achieving a ≥50 % symptom reduction or a decrease of one standard deviation, and the proportion meeting ED cut‑off criteria before and after treatment. Declare therapeutic success when post‑intervention means are significantly lower (p ≤ .05) and effect sizes are medium or large compared with TAU.

steps.title: Conduct cost‑effectiveness and cost‑utility analyses
steps.instruction: Calculate incremental cost‑effectiveness ratios (ICERs) and incremental cost‑utility ratios (ICURs) using the EQ‑5D‑5L to derive quality‑adjusted life years (QALYs). Do not apply discounting because follow‑up does not exceed 12 months. Use bootstrapping to obtain confidence intervals for ICERs and ICURs. Analyse missing data with Student’s t‑tests and χ² tests for severity level, sex and age. Perform a sensitivity analysis to test robustness of cost‑effectiveness and cost‑utility results.
